title: Exercise 1 – Valmont SA
text: Valmont SA pays one dividend per year on 31 December. In June 2024, Valmont did a 2-for-1 stock split (2 new shares for 1 old share). The table shows the closing prices and the dividends per share paid on each date; prices and dividends from 2024 on are per new share.

title: Exercise 2 – Aurora and Borealis
text: You invest EUR 12,000 in Aurora SE and EUR 8,000 in Borealis ASA. The returns of the two stocks have a correlation of 0.2.

title: Exercise 3 – Fund North and Fund South
text: You want to invest EUR 10,000 in one of two well-diversified funds, combined with the risk-free asset. You can borrow and lend at the risk-free rate of 3%.

title: Exercise 5 – Lumière SA and the four-factor model
text: Lumière SA is a listed media company. The risk-free rate is 2%. The table shows the expected premium of each factor portfolio and Lumière's beta with each factor; Lumière's market beta in the CAPM is also 1.1.

title: Exercise 6 – Fjord ASA
text: Fjord ASA has a market capitalization of EUR 900 million and EUR 300 million of debt (no excess cash). Its bonds have a yield to maturity of 6%; debt with Fjord's rating has an average annual default rate of 2% and investors lose 50% of the value in default. Fjord's equity beta is 1.3, the risk-free rate is 2.5% and the market risk premium is 5%. The corporate tax rate is 25%.

title: Exercise 7 – Saline AG
text: Saline AG is all-equity financed, with 50 million shares trading at EUR 40 and an (unlevered) cost of capital of 10%. Saline borrows EUR 800 million of risk-free debt at 4% and uses the money to repurchase shares at the market price. Assume perfect capital markets.
